---
title: "Hackathon 4"
subtitle: "Bringing research tools to Galaxy"
---

This hackathon will be held on 11 December at [SURF](https://www.surf.nl/en) in Amsterdam. It will **bring together** tool developers and users to **make research tools available in [Galaxy](https://usegalaxy.org)**, the open-source web platform for accessible, reproducible data analysis.

The day opens with an **introduction to Galaxy**. After that, the rest of the day is dedicated to **hands-on work**: participants bring a tool they know well and work on packaging it for Galaxy, so that researchers can run it through a web interface and combine it with other tools in Galaxy workflows.

## Who should attend

The hackathon is intended for **developers and users of research tools** who want to make their tool easier to use and combine with other tools. Participants should be:

* **Comfortable with programming**.
* **Familiar with the Linux command line**, at least at a basic level.
* **Very familiar with the tool** they want to package.
* **Familiar with [SURF Research Cloud](https://www.surf.nl/en/services/surf-research-cloud)**, or willing to join a preparatory workshop on 29 November or 5 December.

## Bring your own tool

Participants work on a tool of their own choosing. You can be the developer of the tool or a user of it, and you can register to work on more than one tool. To be a good fit for Galaxy, the tool should:

* **Be command-line based**, not graphical user interface based.
* **Take one of the [supported datatypes](https://usegalaxy.org/datatypes) as input.**
* **Run on Linux (Ubuntu).**
* **Have a workable software license.** See the [licensing outreach](1licensing_outreach.qmd) for why this matters.
